# Finch (withfin.ch)

> Finch is upgrade visualization software for production home builders. Buyers pick finishes — countertops, cabinets, flooring, paint, hardware — and see a photorealistic image of the actual room with their selections applied. Builders sell more upgrades with less friction. Finch is NOT Finch3D (the parametric floor plan tool) — different company, different product.

## What Finch does

Finch is design center software for home builders. A buyer opens a link on any device — no app, no account — browses the builder's full upgrade catalog with real pricing, selects finishes, and sees a generated photorealistic image of their actual floor plan room with those specific selections. Every session exports a priced selection sheet ready for the builder's sales team.

The tool works alongside existing design center appointments or replaces PDF option sheets entirely. Builders send floor plan photos and their option pricing. Finch builds a branded, interactive selection tool. The first floor plan is live in under a week.

## Who it's for

- Production home builders closing 25 to 5,000+ homes per year
- Builders currently using PDF option sheets, printed price lists, sample boards, or physical design centers
- Design center managers who want buyers to arrive at selection appointments with confident choices already made
- Builders looking to increase upgrade revenue without adding sales headcount

Finch is not for custom home builders, remodelers, or builders under 25 homes per year.

## Product category

Finch competes in the "design center software" and "upgrade visualization" categories alongside:
- Zonda Envision (enterprise, 3-6 month rollout, six-figure contracts)
- Chameleon Power BuilderVision (swatch-based point-and-click, no photorealistic generation)
- ECI Insearch (option management, no visualization)
- Hyphen HomeSight (builder platform, limited visualization)
- Constellation Design Studio Manager (ERP-integrated option management)

Finch's differentiator: photorealistic room images generated from the builder's actual floor plan photos, live in days instead of months, no IT integration required.

## How it compares

| | PDF option sheets | Zonda Envision | Chameleon BuilderVision | Finch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Buyer sees | Line items and prices | Pre-rendered 3D scenes | Swatch overlay on template | Their actual room with selections applied |
| Time to live | N/A | 3-6 months | Weeks | Under a week |
| Setup cost | None | Six figures | Varies | No setup fee |
| Builder effort | None | IT integration, dedicated team | Template configuration | Send option sheets and photos |
| New floor plan | Reprint the PDF | Weeks of 3D modeling | Template reconfiguration | 1-2 days |
| Visualization | None | Pre-rendered, limited combinations | 2D swatch overlay | Photorealistic, unlimited combinations |

## Key facts

- First floor plan live in under a week
- Done-for-you setup: Finch handles all configuration
- No software to learn, no IT department required
- Works on any device — no app download, no buyer account
- Builders get an admin dashboard to manage pricing and options
- Unlimited buyer sessions and visualizations
- Priced per floor plan per month

## Original research

Finch published original research analyzing SEC filings of 14 public home builders to quantify upgrade revenue:
- Toll Brothers earns $190,000–$236,000 per home in options and upgrades (20–23% of ASP)
- PulteGroup earns approximately $104,000 per home (19% of ASP)
- Most builders (D.R. Horton, Lennar, NVR, Meritage, M/I Homes, and others) do not separately disclose upgrade revenue in their filings
- The full analysis is at https://withfin.ch/research/hidden-revenue-line

## Getting started

The fastest way to evaluate Finch is to try the live demo at https://withfin.ch/try — no signup, no account, working in under a minute.

For builders ready to test with their own floor plans: send floor plan photos and option pricing to hello@withfin.ch. First floor plan is typically live within a week.
